sessionName: Week 5 - Pipeline architecture for two motions
summary: Luke Badiali worked with Simon Clarke and Priya Natarajan on pipeline design. DD and 100-day plans behave very differently, and the current pipeline mixes them. We agreed two separate pipelines with their own stages, and a weekly review of stalled 100-day plan opportunities.

discussion.keyPoints: Simon's export showed DD and post-deal work in one list, making the pipeline look healthier than it is. Many DD opportunities are deals that never progressed.
Priya said DD runs 2 to 4 weeks from instruction to readout, while 100-day plans take 6 to 10 weeks to sign. Lost deals often happen when the fund's own deal falls away.
Only about 1 in 5 DD engagements currently turns into a 100-day plan. Simon wants that doubled.

recommendations.recommendation: Run two pipelines: DD (Panel enquiry, Instructed, Readout, Closed) and 100-day plan (Readout briefing, Proposal, Signed), with exit criteria for each.
Raise DD to 100-day plan conversion from 1 in 5 to 2 in 5 within a year.
Review 100-day plan opportunities with no movement for 21 days at a weekly Monday pipeline call.
Hold 2.5 times next quarter's post-deal revenue target in the 100-day plan pipeline.

actions.action: Split the current pipeline export into the two pipelines

nextFocus: Set up CRM, data and forecasting to support the two pipelines.
nextPreparation: Simon to confirm which systems hold client and fund contacts today.

tests.question: What pipelines did we agree to run?
What conversion target did we set from DD to 100-day plans?
Is the weekly review of stalled 100-day plan deals agreed?
